items.raw_snippet:
A similar pattern has emerged in this year’s equity initial public offering (IPO) market. AI and related infrastructure companies account for more than 80% of cumulative IPO value, driven in large part by huge offerings from SpaceX and Anthropic. More broadly, eight of the ten largest IPOs in 2026 are in the AI-related space when including industrial, energy, and utility companies tied to data center development. [...] # AI has dominated the IPO market this year

Markets & Economy

If one word captures artificial intelligence’s impact on the economy, it is “dominant”. In the first three quarters of this year, AI-related investment accounted for about two-thirds of GDP growth.1 More than 40% of investment-grade bond issuance so far this year has come from AI-focused companies – roughly double the share two years ago.2 [...] Meanwhile, AI-related IPOs have mostly fared poorly since trading in the secondary market. The table below shows returns for the thirteen AI-themed firms that raised at least $1 billion in their IPOs. Twelve are trading below their offering price, with an average return of -32%.

items.raw_snippet:
Member-only story

# The AI Boom Has a Hidden Money Loop. Here’s How It Works.

CodeTune

Some of the world’s largest technology companies are financing the very businesses that purchase their products. Understanding this relationship changes how we interpret the extraordinary numbers behind the AI boom.

If not a Medium member? CLICK HERE

On February 27, 2026, Amazon announced two enormous financial commitments involving OpenAI.

The first was a $50 billion investment in the AI company. [...] The second was an agreement under which OpenAI would expand its existing $38 billion cloud contract with Amazon Web Services by another $100 billion over eight years.

Read those announcements separately, and they tell two familiar stories. Amazon is investing in a promising technology company, and AWS is securing a major customer.

Read them together, and something more interesting emerges. [...] Amazon is providing capital to a company that has committed to spending substantial amounts of money on Amazon’s own infrastructure.

The money moves in both directions.

Amazon is not alone in establishing these arrangements. Nvidia, Microsoft, and other major technology companies participate in variations of the same financial structure.

items.snippet: AI consulting is advisory work that helps a business decide how to use artificia...
items.raw_snippet:
AI consulting is advisory work that helps a business decide how to use artificial intelligence and then put that decision into practice. An AI consultant looks at how your company works today, finds the tasks where AI can save time or money, recommends tools, and guides the first rollout. [...] | Freelance AI business consultant | Small businesses, single projects | Lowest cost, flexible | Quality varies a lot; check references |
| Vendor implementation partner | Companies already on a platform | Deep knowledge of one product | May recommend only that vendor's tools |
| Fractional chief AI officer | Growing firms without an AI lead | Ongoing ownership a few days a month | Needs clear goals or becomes a costly advisor | [...] At the large end, some firms run dedicated AI practices. McKinsey's QuantumBlack, AI by McKinsey, for example, describes itself as blending AI and engineering with "deep strategic thinking and domain expertise," and joined McKinsey in 2015 as a 45-person start-up. Firms of that size suit enterprises; most small businesses get better value from a freelancer or boutique.
